entry_sequence.action: I set my time zone to New York. So, that's UTC minus 4
I then look for the 9:30 candle, which is the market open in New York
I'm going to mark out the high and the low. So, I mark the high and then do the same thing with the low. This gives me my opening range
After that, I'm just waiting for a candle to break out through this range

I prefer to wait for the candle to actually break through and then close above. So, in this case, my signal is this candle here because it's the first one to actually break out and then close outside of that range
I then enter at the open of the next one

confluences.description: I don't trade after the 12:00 candle, which would be here. So that would be my cut off for entering a trade
I also don't trade ranges that are either too small or too big based on the recent ATR

targets.description: I target 1.5 to one reward to risk

stop.anchor: the stop loss goes at the bottom of the range

entry_sequence.action: First, I switch over to the 5-minut chart. This way, I can react to price action a lot quicker.
My orb range is still defined by the first 15 minutes of the day. But since I'm on the 5-minut time frame now, I have to use the first three candles to define my range high and range low.

Once I have those defined, I then wait for my breakout just like before. But this time, I don't buy immediately on the close of this breakout candle. Instead, I have to wait and see if price is going to make a pullback towards the opening range.
what I'm looking for is a candle that's going to break through the range but then close back above it, which is exactly what this candle here has done.

Once I get this pullback candle, I don't enter immediately. I want to see confirmation that price is going to bounce off and move back up. And I'm going to be waiting for a break of this most recent high. We get that on the next candle. And this gives me my confirmation to enter into a trade. So, the trade is opened here.

confluences.description: I need to take into account the height of this breakout. And I made sure that this was greater than at least 1 times ATR to be considered a suitable breakout.
The reason for this is that I want to see buyers coming back in and pushing the price back up. That gives me confirmation that this line is now starting to act as support.

targets.description: I will target 1 and 1/2 times for my take-profit ratio.
I tested take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2 in increments of 0.5.

stop.anchor: The stop loss will still go at the bottom of my opening range.
